Split the conjunction.

1. Convert the polynomial bound \(\|f(n)\|\le Cn^x\) for \(n\ge1\) into absolute convergence of the Dirichlet series whenever \(\operatorname{re}(s)>x+1\). Indeed,
\[
\|f(n)n^{-s}\|\le Cn^{x-\operatorname{re}(s)},
\]
and the resulting \(p\)-series is summable. Then apply the characterization of `LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv` to obtain
\(\operatorname{abscissaOfAbsConv}(f)\le x+1\), taking care only of the `EReal` coercions.

2. Prove the convolution identity by function extensionality and unfold `LSeries.convolution`. For \(n>0\), complete multiplicativity gives
\[
\chi(d)\chi(n/d)=\chi(n)
\]
for every divisor \(d\mid n\). Thus the divisor sum becomes
\[
\chi(n)\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d).
\]
Use the standard von Mangoldt divisor-sum identity
\(\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)=\log n\), then transport the real logarithm through `Complex.ofReal`. Handle \(n=0\) separately; both sides vanish under the relevant definitions.
